claims.statement: The how-to declares FPT/GHEC/GHES with plan/visibility-dependent protected-branch availability; managing rules requires repository admin or a custom edit-repository-rules permission, not merely write access.

Classic rules can target named, current/future or wildcard branches. FNM_PATHNAME means star does not match slash; qa/* is one level, while qa/**/* is recursive. Example names are not adopted target scopes.
An exact-name classic rule outranks patterned rules; among repeated identical exact names the earliest wins, and rules with special characters are applied oldest first.
A higher-priority exact-name rule can make an exception. Only one classic rule applies, unlike rulesets; enterprise cross-repository and conversion links retain their feature gates.
A protected branch need not yet exist when its rule is created; bypass-list actors are supported only for organization-owned repositories.

Navigate to the repository Settings (More menu if hidden), then Branches, add a classic rule and enter the branch-name pattern. FPT/GHEC and GHES sidebar labels differ; these are UI instructions, not executed changes.
Pull requests and approvals are separately optional: select Require a pull request, then optionally Require approvals and choose the approval count. The source does not choose a universal quorum.
The included mergeability note preserves the exact-GitHub-generated-merge exception for manual pushes and invalidation after merge-base content changes when stale/latest-push settings are enabled.
Optional stale approval dismissal applies when code-modifying commits are pushed; selecting it is not proof of native rejection behavior.
Optional Code Owners review accepts any one of multiple owners of affected code, rather than requiring every listed owner.
Selected actors may bypass required pull requests; organization repositories can restrict review dismissal to selected actors. Record both paths when evaluating effective protection.
Optional approval of the latest reviewable push must be by someone other than its pusher.
Optional required checks have explicit selected names; up-to-date-before-merge is a separate option for testing against latest protected-branch code.
Conversation resolution is an optional setting distinct from approvals and code-owner review.
Required signing and linear history are separate optional settings; applicability and compatible delivery methods still require deliberate policy decisions.
Merge queue and successful deployment to chosen environments are optional settings; their navigation references do not certify live queue or environment behavior.
Lock branch can optionally allow fork syncing; no-bypass is a separate option. These settings must be composed with other rules.
For eligible organization plans/visibility, restrict push actors and optionally restrict matching-branch creation, choosing people/teams/apps for those grants.
Optional force pushes can admit every writer including administrators or selected actors, retaining the source’s linked constraints.
Allow deletions is an optional setting; clicking Create saves the configured classic rule. This procedure was read, not executed.
To edit, use the repository Settings/Branches route, Edit the rule, change desired settings and Save changes; the source supplies no observed readback.
To delete a classic rule, use Settings/Branches and Delete beside that rule; permission to follow a source instruction is not authorization to remove this estate’s protection.
